clue.text: Salmonella primarily around raw chicken

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word Salmonella

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around or approximately
raw skin is red and sore

explanation.surface: A food-safety warning: undercooked chicken carries salmonella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like part of the food scare, but it is the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone chicken means they are cowardly or frightened, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Snake in hole there has shed its skin

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening or hole

indicators.note: a word that sheds its skin loses its outer letters, so only the inside of there is kept

explanation.surface: A snake has moulted its skin inside a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' is a verb here, not the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to move sinuously, gliding or sliding along, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Serious wound for joiner in hospital department?

indicators.note: for means one thing takes the place of another, here the wound replacing the joiner

parts.note: A&E is the accident and emergency department of a British hospital
the ampersand in A&E stands for and, a conjunction that joins words
a cut is a wound

explanation.surface: A wounded carpenter turns up at casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British emergency room; replace its ampersand (the 'joiner', not a carpenter) with CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious condition or shortage is an acute one: severe and critical.

clue.text: Last old male seduced by Olive?

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: being seduced by someone means being taken in by them, so the male goes inside the tree

parts.note: an olive is an example of a tree, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A former lover's final fling: an old man seduced by a woman called Olive.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive looks like a woman's name; it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means furthest or outermost, so it can stand for last, as in the extreme end.

clue.text: He tells cricketer to get runs

parts.note: Shane Warne was a famous Australian leg-spin bowler
R is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone reports a cricketer for being told to score runs.
explanation.definitionFit: One who warns tells others of danger, so a person who tells is a warner.

clue.text: Antique piece of furniture without Mr Chippendale's initial

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters of Mr are removed from the furniture

parts.note: an armchair is a piece of furniture
taken as written, the letters M and R

indicators.note: initial asks for the first letter of Chippendale's

explanation.surface: An antique Chippendale piece described as lacking the maker's initial.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M and R (scattered) from ARMCHAIR to leave ARCHAI, then add C. Thomas Chippendale was a famous 18th-century English furniture maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique and archaic are synonyms: both mean very old or belonging to an earlier age.

clue.text: Best single by group?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the single sits next to the group

parts.note: a number can mean a group of people, as in one of our number
one means single

explanation.surface: A question about a band's finest single.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a chart-topping single, itself another sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The number one is the top or best of something, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Dismissal of place for meetings with daughter

parts.note: Redcar, a North Yorkshire town, has a racecourse that holds race meetings

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissed from a meeting venue along with their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meetings' are horse-race meetings: Redcar is a seaside town in north-east England with a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee shows a red card to send a player off the field, which is a dismissal.

clue.text: Happen to order sandwiches and sweet

indicators.note: sandwiches means encloses between two layers, so the order goes round the happening

parts.note: to sort is to order or arrange
to be is to happen or take place, as in so be it

explanation.surface: Someone happens to order sandwiches and a pudding at a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food on the menu, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a sweet is a dessert, and sorbet is a frozen fruit dessert.

clue.text: Friends say Tom indicates you must go out

indicators.note: letters that must go out are thrown out of their places, so the words Tom indicates you are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tom tells you your friends must go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Friends as an example, so it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends, the long-running American TV series, is an example of a sitcom.

clue.text: Tall actor removing line for hotel food

indicators.note: removing one letter for another means it is taken out and swapped for the replacement

parts.note: John Cleese, of Monty Python and Fawlty Towers, is famously tall
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tall actor gives up his lines for hotel food.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers, Cleese's sitcom, is set in a hotel, which aids the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is a food made from milk curds, an example of the category.

clue.text: Stop with this playboy in bachelor flat?

indicators.note: in means the playboy is placed inside the bachelor's flat

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree
a pad is slang for a flat or home
a rake is a playboy or womaniser

explanation.surface: A playboy is told to stop his antics in his bachelor pad.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake pad is the component pressed against a disc to stop a vehicle.

clue.text: Tabloid workers filling in newspaper piece

indicators.note: filling in means occupying the inside of the newspaper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid newspaper
men can mean workers, as in the boss and his men

explanation.surface: Tabloid staff fill in at a broadsheet to write a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small piece broken off something, a synonym.

clue.text: Mix egg in; turn to make biscuit

indicators.note: a baking instruction: mix means the letters of egg in and turn are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe step: mix in the egg, turn the dough, and you have a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger nut is a hard, ginger-flavoured British biscuit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Pieces of music from guys on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: guys are ropes or cords, as in guy ropes holding a tent

explanation.surface: Some blokes play music on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' looks like men, but it is the tent ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chords are groups of notes played together, loosely the building pieces of music.

clue.text: Caught a breath, lying back for rest

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: lying back means the word is laid backwards

parts.note: a pant is a short gasping breath

explanation.surface: Someone catches their breath and lies back for a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short, light sleep, a kind of rest.

clue.text: Military land here in area Serbia lost

indicators.note: lost means astray or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Military forces land in a region that Serbia lost.
explanation.definitionFit: An air base is where military aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Prince with sick queen to hold out

parts.note: feeling off means feeling unwell or sick
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A prince with an ill queen holds out.
explanation.definitionFit: To proffer is to offer or hold something out for acceptance.

clue.text: Mix fuel source that's key to get energy

parts.note: coal is a fuel
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fuel blended with a key ingredient produces energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to come together and merge, a synonym for mix or combine.

clue.text: Profit from account, having turnover go up

indicators.note: having turnover means turned over, so the account's letters are reversed

parts.note: to shin up is to climb or go up

explanation.surface: A business boosts profits from an account as its turnover rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business revenue but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in on something is to take advantage of or profit from it, an idiom.

clue.text: Out of money — working in topless magazines with model

indicators.note: with means one piece is placed alongside the other
in means the money and the working go inside
topless means the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: mags is short for magazines
on means working or operating, as in the machine is on
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A broke model works in topless magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: MON goes in AGS (MAGS less its top), then add T.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst means in the company of, as in one out of many: one amongst many.

clue.text: Body keeps appearing in crime drama on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means one piece sits after the other
appearing in means one piece shows up inside another

parts.note: CSI: Crime Scene Investigation is a TV crime drama
to keep something is to have it

explanation.surface: A dead body keeps turning up in a Sunday crime drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' suggests a corpse in the drama; it is the frame of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the frame or body of a vehicle on which the rest is mounted.

clue.text: Serious? You for French after German, religious studies and English

indicators.note: after means the French word comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is the British school subject of religious studies
vous is the French word for you

explanation.surface: A language student asks whether a lesson of French, German, RS and English is serious.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (religious instruction) is the old name of the school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievous injury or offence is a serious one, as in grievous bodily harm.

clue.text: Child that's left hospital: men criticise nurses

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: nurses means holds or cradles, so the hospital goes inside

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a critic pans a show

explanation.surface: A child discharged from hospital as staff criticise the nurses.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphan is a child whose parents have died, one left behind alone.

clue.text: Beat United and regularly lose in games

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the games

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word lose

explanation.surface: A football report: beat United, who regularly lose matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like a verb for defeating United; it is the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the regular beat of blood through the arteries.

clue.text: One blows things up in film, saying gang's sorry

indicators.note: sorry means in a sorry or wretched state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang in a film apologises after blowing things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows things up' suggests explosives; it means enlarging.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens for magnifying makes small objects look bigger, figuratively enlarging them.

clue.text: Comes in and puts on record

definitions.meaning: goes into a room or place
writes data into a register or log

explanation.definitionFit: The verb has both senses: to go in, and to record data such as entering figures in a ledger.

clue.text: Trouble as married one dropped off lover

indicators.note: dropped off means removed from the front of the word

parts.note: a mistress is a lover
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A married man drops off his lover, causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress means strain or pressure, so trouble and worry are close synonyms.
